quests.instruction: Touch the container we pack with food to eat at school!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: It usually has a lid or a zipper to keep food fresh.
quests.explanation: Well done! A lunchbox keeps a sandwich, fruit, or snack fresh and safe.
quests.funFact: Some lunchboxes have special cool packs inside to keep food fresh and cold!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the helper who takes care of us when we feel sick!
quests.question: School Nurse
quests.hint: This helper checks on you if you feel sick or get a small bump.
quests.explanation: That's right! We visit the school nurse for a bump, scrape, or tummy ache.
quests.funFact: A school nurse often keeps a cozy cot ready for students who need a short rest!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the room where clapping and singing fill the air!
quests.question: Music Room
quests.hint: You visit this room to sing songs or try a new instrument.
quests.explanation: Yes! The music room is where students sing songs and play instruments.
quests.funFact: A music room might have drums, a piano, and even small xylophones to try!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person who teaches your class every day!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: This person helps you learn new things and checks your work.
quests.explanation: Well done! A teacher guides the whole class through every lesson.
quests.funFact: Teachers often spend extra time planning fun lessons for their whole class!

quests.instruction: Touch the pen with bright, bold ink that we use for coloring!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: If you leave its cap off too long, it can dry out.
quests.explanation: Well done! A marker's ink is thicker and darker than a pencil's.
quests.funFact: Markers can dry out if you forget to put the cap back on!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the practice work we finish at home!
quests.question: Homework
quests.hint: You usually do this after school, not during class time.
quests.explanation: That's right! We complete homework at home to practice what we learned.
quests.funFact: Doing a little homework each day can help new lessons stick in your memory!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the room where messy hands mean a masterpiece is being made!
quests.question: Art Room
quests.hint: You visit this room to paint pictures or make fun crafts.
quests.explanation: Yes! The art room is where students paint pictures and make colorful crafts.
quests.funFact: Art rooms often have sinks nearby so students can wash paint off their hands!

quests.instruction: Find the word for another student who sits and learns beside you!
quests.question: Classmate
quests.hint: You might sit next to this person or share a table with them.
quests.explanation: Well done! A classmate can become a great friend during the school year.
quests.funFact: Working with a classmate on a project is a great way to learn together!

quests.instruction: Point to the item that comes in little pots of many colors!
quests.question: Paint
quests.hint: You need a brush to spread it smoothly across your page.
quests.explanation: That's right! We dip a brush in paint to color a picture.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people made paint from crushed rocks, plants, and even berries!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the subject where blank paper turns into your very own story!
quests.question: Writing
quests.hint: You practice holding a pencil carefully during this subject.
quests.explanation: Yes! Writing is the subject where we practice letters, sentences, and stories.
quests.funFact: Learning to write neatly takes practice, just like learning to read does!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the place with slides and swings at school!
quests.question: Playground
quests.hint: You visit this place during recess to play with your friends.
quests.explanation: Well done! A playground gives students a fun place to play outside.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds have slides, swings, and climbing bars all in one place!

quests.instruction: Point to the item that keeps your homework neat inside your backpack!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It has no pages of its own, but it holds other papers inside.
quests.explanation: That's right! We slide our worksheets into a folder to keep them tidy.
quests.funFact: Colorful folders can help students quickly find the right subject for each class!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the part of the day when we all eat!
quests.question: Lunchtime
quests.hint: This is the part of the day when every student stops to eat.
quests.explanation: That's right! We open our lunchbox and eat together at lunchtime.
quests.funFact: Lunchtime often comes right in the middle of the school day, giving everyone energy!

quests.instruction: Find the item that comes in a big stack, ready for writing!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: It is thin, flat, and usually white or another light color.
quests.explanation: Yes! Paper is the flat sheet we write, draw, and color on.
quests.funFact: Most paper today is made from trees that are grown just for that purpose!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the room where visitors check in first!
quests.question: Office
quests.hint: Visitors usually stop here first when they arrive at school.
quests.explanation: That's right! We visit the office if we arrive late or need help.
quests.funFact: The school office often keeps important papers safe for every single student!

quests.instruction: Find the soft tool that fixes a mistake without tearing your paper!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: Pencils often carry a tiny piece of it on their top end.
quests.explanation: Correct! An eraser is a student's best friend when a letter looks wrong.
quests.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people used soft bread to rub out pencil marks!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for a person who comes to school to learn!
quests.question: Student
quests.hint: This person listens to the teacher and practices new skills.
quests.explanation: Well done! Every child in a classroom is a student, just like you.
quests.funFact: Students all around the world go to school to learn new things every day!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the subject where a puzzle of numbers waits to be solved!
quests.question: Math
quests.hint: You practice adding and subtracting during this class.
quests.explanation: Yes! Math is the subject where we count, add, and solve number problems.
quests.funFact: Math is used everywhere, from counting your toys to telling the time!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool we always use carefully to cut along a line!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: You put your fingers in its handles and squeeze to make it cut.
quests.explanation: Well done! Scissors help us cut paper into new shapes for our projects.
quests.funFact: The very first scissors were shaped very differently from the ones we use today!

quests.instruction: Touch the furniture we pull up to the table before we sit down!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: You pull it out before you sit down at your desk.
quests.explanation: Well done! A chair gives every student a comfy place to sit.
quests.funFact: Chairs have been used by people for thousands of years, even in ancient times!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin wooden tool that makes a mark when you write with it!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: You need to sharpen its tip so it can write again.
quests.explanation: Correct! Every student uses a pencil to practice writing every day.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people wrote with sticks and feathers before pencils were invented!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the happy time when we go outside to play!
quests.question: Recess
quests.hint: This is a short, happy break from lessons spent outside.
quests.explanation: That's right! We run, play, and have fun with friends during recess.
quests.funFact: Recess helps students feel refreshed and ready to learn again afterward!

quests.instruction: Touch the smooth board where today's lesson is written for everyone to see!
quests.question: Whiteboard
quests.hint: It hangs at the front of the classroom for everyone to see.
quests.explanation: Yes! A whiteboard is the smooth board where a teacher writes each lesson.
quests.funFact: Whiteboard markers wipe away easily, unlike regular permanent markers!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the vehicle that picks up students every morning!
quests.question: School Bus
quests.hint: It stops along a route each morning to pick up students.
quests.explanation: Well done! A school bus has room for many students to ride together.
quests.funFact: School buses are often painted bright yellow so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the leader who helps every teacher and student!
quests.question: Principal
quests.hint: This person's office often welcomes visitors who come to the school.
quests.explanation: Well done! A principal makes sure the whole school runs smoothly.
quests.funFact: A principal often visits many classrooms in just one single school day!

quests.instruction: Touch the flat tool with numbers that helps us draw straight lines!
quests.question: Ruler
quests.hint: It can tell you how many centimeters long your pencil is.
quests.explanation: Well done! A ruler has numbers that show us the length of things.
quests.funFact: Rulers can measure in centimeters on one side and inches on the other!

quests.instruction: Point to the word for the room filled with students and desks!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: Your teacher and your classmates spend most of the day here with you.
quests.explanation: That's right! A classroom has desks, chairs, and a board for lessons.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms have cozy reading corners with soft cushions for story time!

quests.instruction: Point to the pouch that keeps your desk neat and tidy!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It holds your pencils, eraser, and ruler all in one place.
quests.explanation: Correct! A pencil case travels inside your backpack with all your tools.
quests.funFact: A tidy pencil case can help you find your pencil in just one second!

quests.instruction: Point to the stick that can be wiped away with a dry cloth!
quests.question: Chalk
quests.hint: It feels a little dusty and can leave marks on your fingers.
quests.explanation: That's right! Chalk leaves a soft mark that a cloth can wipe away.
quests.funFact: Outdoor chalk lets children draw colorful pictures right on the sidewalk!

quests.instruction: Touch the table where your pencils and notebook sit during class!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: A chair usually sits right beside it, ready for you to sit down.
quests.explanation: Well done! A desk gives every student their own space to work.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms use desks that can be pushed together to make small groups!
